To get me to pay $171 (at the time of writing this review) for a skincare product, it needs to have way more than 3 ingredients that I consider superstar ingredients.

Plus, there’s 4 different silicones and alcohol in this product, which is pretty unacceptable for a skincare product at this price point.

There’s also fragrance in it. It’s the last ingredient. It has a very faint smell. I can’t quite place it. Kind of perfume scented, but very faint.

In the end, I just don’t see where they come up with the price point for this. I feel that way about a lot of the so-called “big name brand” products, where just because they’re a well-known brand, they feel it justifies slapping a bigger price on it, even when the ingredients and/or results don’t seem to justify it. But, this brand isn’t even a known brand, unless you’re a small spa or boutique as far as I can tell. So, that definitely doesn’t justify the price (not that I think it would even if it was a well known brand). But, the ingredients also don’t justify the price. There isn’t enough superstar type ingredients in this to justify the price. There’s a bunch of basic good ingredients, and a few superstar, and then some not great ingredients like fragrance, alcohol, and different silicones. I find that unacceptable when you’re trying to charge this much. Not to mention, they claim results occur in 7 days. I used this for a month and didn’t see any results at all. I don’t even feel like it provides much hydration. It just feels silky smooth on the skin...thanks to the silicones. So, I don’t recommend this.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Works okay if you can draw line fast and get lashes on it, and line has to be thick
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
A while back I tried an adhesive eyeliner for the first time. I had never heard of it before, so I honestly thought it was going to just be a gimmicky product and not actually work. I figured if something like that actually worked, why hadn’t I heard of it already?! I mean, lash glue can be a pain to work with. To have an eyeliner and lash glue in one, that’s amazing! That seemed like something people would be raving about, but I hadn’t even heard such a thing existed. But, I figured I’d try it out. I’m glad I did! That one actually worked well. It did end up drying out fast, but it worked. So, since then, I have been trying out different ones.

This has a felt tip. The eyeliner is pigmented, very black. The adhesive is sticky, but not extremely sticky. You have to work pretty darn fast with this. I have really small, really hooded eyes. So, when I wear liner, I like to tight line my lash line. I don’t want to be taking up the tiny lid space that’s actually seen with black liner. In order to tightline with a really thin line like I like, I usually move pretty slowly. Unfortunately, I can’t do that with this liner. I have to move fast if I don’t want it to dry and lose its stickiness. But, even if I move fast, the thin line like I like doesn’t cut it. The liner doesn’t seem all that sticky. But, it can be....

I always want to test adhesive liners before applying them to my eye. I don’t know if I’ll have some sort of reaction, so I figure it’s better to be safe than sorry. So, I draw a little line of it in my forearm. While I’m doing that, I give the liner a little test to see how it works. I drew the little line on my forearm. Then, I took a lash and stuck it to that line. The lash stuck really well to the line. It stayed on it well, even when I gave it little tugs. After that, I was really excited to try it on my eyes! I didn’t have any sort of reaction to the liner, so it was time to try it on my eyes....

I drew a thin line on my eyes, grabbed the lash and went to apply it. It stuck great to the last part of the line I had just finished drawing, but wouldn’t stick to the area where I started drawing the line. I didn’t know why, so I wiped it off and tried again. The same thing happened. Then, I figured it probably dried quickly, so I needed to work faster. So, I had everything ready to go and drew the line quickly, then went to apply the lash. That time it stuck a little better and actually stuck to whole line, but it kept lifting. I finally got it figured out where it would stick well - I had to draw a thicker line and had to be quick. Unfortunately, I don’t like thick liner, so it just won’t work for me.

Overall, the liner works well if you’re able to work very fast and like thicker liner. I only like tight-lining my lashes with a very thin line, so this liner isn’t for me. But, like I said, if you don’t mind thick liner and are able to work fast drawing the line and getting the lashes stuck to it, this could work for you.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Thought this was amazing, but now only like it..read UPDATE at bottom of review
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
I’d been using the Sol De Janeiro Bum Bum Body Scrub. I looooove that scrub. It smells AMAZING and the smell stays with you. You know how most body scrubs smell nice but as soon as you’re done using it, you can’t really smell it on you? Well, the Bum Bum Body Scrub isn’t like that! You can smell it on you after, heck, my whole apartment smells like coconut after using it! BUUUUT it’s $42 and it’s a sugar scrub so it goes FAST. I also hate the container it comes in. It’s cute, but it’s a pain to open in the shower, get your hand in there and get some scrub out, and it dissolves pretty quick as water hits it since it’s a sugar scrub. So, I wanted a sugar scrub that was more affordable, but still smelled great, that wasn’t such a pain to get out in the shower, and that possibly didn’t dissolve so quick when water hit it. THIS SCRUB CHECKS ALL THOSE BOXES!

It’s way more affordable than the Bum Bum scrub. It comes in a jar, so you have to screw the top off, similar to the Bum Bum scrub. But, a lot easier. It smells amazing, like vanilla. It isn’t as strong smelling as the Bum Bum scrub, but I still feel like I can smell it on me after my shower. The BEST part....this is a “Sugar Balm Body Scrub.” The balm makes it kind of like a thicker, kind of paste. It is easier to pick up with your hands, spread on your body, and it doesn’t dissolve anywhere close to as quick as most sugar scrubs.

Overall, I LOVE this scrub! I will definitely replace it when I run out, and definitely recommend it!

UPDATE - The first few times I used this, I don’t know how I didn’t notice. But, when I was using it again, I saw a loose hair from my head on my arm, I went to pick it up and as I did, my nails kind of scraped against my skin. I felt gunk go under my nails. I looked and saw all this gunk under the 2 nails that scraped against my skin! I was like, “WHAT THE HECK?!” So, then I took my nails and scraped against another area I’d used the scrub at and the same thing happened. I remembered people saying this left a film on their skin, which at the time I initially wrote my review I didn’t feel it did. But, now I DEFINITELY say it does. BUT, it can be washed off. After I scraped my skin and found out about the gunk, I took a regular body wash on a wash cloth and went over the areas I’d used the scrub. After that I scraped my nails over the areas again and, thankfully, no gunk. So, you can get the residue off. Now, whether or not you want to go through scrubbing your body with this scrub and then go over it again with soap or body wash, that’s up to you. For me, it’s not a big deal because I like how this is a balm that doesn’t rinse away as quickly as a regular sugar scrub does. I like that I can spread it onto my body and then scrub without worrying about it melting away as soon as it touches my skin. So, I’m okay dealing with having to go over the areas with a body wash after using it. But, I’m definitely going to keep searching to find the perfect body sugar scrub that is affordable and doesn’t melt away quickly like this one, but that doesn’t leave a film I have to wash off after using it. So, I’m dropping my rating down from a 5 to a 3. I thought about only dropping it to a 4 since I still like it and am willing to deal with having to go over and wash again where I used it. But, it is still kind of a pain to have to do, so I decided to drop it to a 3.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Gear combo! Cleans skin, doesn’t dry it out, helps keep away & heal blemishes and marks left behind!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This is a great combo! I’ve honestly come to not expect too much out of so-called acne treatment regimens. For the most part, they either don’t do anything beyond what my usual skin care does, and if they do help, they end up drying my skin out so bad, I’m not sure which is worse. But, this claims to be effective without causing dryness. It has salicylic acid, retinol, niacinamide, and hyaluronic acid - all ingredients I look for in my skin care, whether it’s acne fighting or not. So, I figured this was worth a try!

I like that this has a regular strength option with 0.2% retinol, which is the one I got, or sensitive strength, which has 0.05% retinol. Most products don’t offer that!

This also contains 2% salicylic acid, 2% hyaluronic acid, and 3% niacinamide!

I’m so glad I tried it! It has simple packaging with easy to read instructions.

This has really helped my skin! I have redness in my skin. No rosacea or anything, my skin isn’t sensitive, but I just have really red skin! I get hormonal breakouts. Sometimes I can keep them away, but most times I get 1 or 2 pimples. On their own, they take forever to go away and always leave behind a red dot that just never seems to go away if left on its own! By time I get rid of one flare up, it’s time for another. It’s a vicious cycle! This combo has helped so much! It has really reduced my redness! I was thinking I just had really red skin, but apparently it was inflammation because this combo has really reduced it! It has helped clear up spots I had from past acne that have been around forever! No matter my skin care regimen, they just never seemed to go away! This combo has helped fade them, and even gotten some to go away already! My skin hasn’t dried out at all! And, I haven’t had a breakout! It’s been great!

It says this is a 30 day supply. I’ve been using it as instructed and feel like I’ll still have plenty left after 30 days. I’m not sure if that means I’m not using enough each time, but it’s working so I’m not mad about it! I’ll definitely be getting more before I run out so I can always have this combo around! I definitely recommend it if you’re having issues with your skin like me!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: A contour powder that’s actually a cool toned contour shade! And works for my pale skin!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This comes bubble wrapped really well. It has a nice outer product box, but there’s no ingredients listed on it. It’s made in Korea.

I got the shade “Light Gray.” I’m pretty pale and I’ve been looking for a good contour powder for a while. Everything I try always is too orange toned or is the right kind of color but too dark for me. When I saw this, it seemed perfect, so I was excited to try it!

The compact is nice. It’s plain matte black with the brand name in shiny black lettering. It’s very simple but sleek. It has a nice weight to it. It doesn’t feel cheap at all, and feels nice and durable.

When you open it, you just pull it open. There’s no indent where you put your finger to grab it, which I thought was odd. But, it opened easy. It has magnetic closure. There’s a nice sized mirror inside (it’s the full size of the lid). The pan size is good too. It takes up basically the whole bottom part of the compact, which is nice to see. There’s many times where I open a compact to see the pan much smaller and some wide border that just is wasted space.

This is a beautiful contour shade! A lot of times I’ll get a powder that claims to be a contour powder, and it’s more like a bronzer shade. When I use a contour powder, I want one that is cool toned and will mimic my natural shadow like it should, not one that is warm like a bronzer. Otherwise, I’d just use my usual bronzer. So, I loved seeing that this was a great contour shade - cool toned. And, it was a good shade for me, not too dark for my pale skin!

The powder works great. It’s finely milled. It applies nicely. It goes on smoothly. It doesn’t look powdery. It applies evenly. It doesn’t cling to dry or textured areas. You can apply a light layer of it or build it up to get a sharper contour. I like that it gives you the ability to change it up how you want it.

Overall, I think this is a great contour powder. The compact is really nice. The powder works beautifully and looks beautiful. I recommend!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Beautiful! Only complaint is white paint over leaves missing in small spots
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text: This is beautiful! The flowers look gorgeous! In my opinion, you wouldn’t even know they’re fake from far away. They feel nice. They’re glued on really well. They don’t feel loose and aren’t lifting at all. My only complaint is that the white paint over the leaves either wasn’t done completely, or more likely, it came off in some spots. There’s a few areas where there isn’t white, and you can see the green (see photos). It’s not a huge deal because I don’t think it’s noticeable unless you’re looking closely.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Huge liners! Beautiful colors!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
I was expecting these to come together in a small box or something similar. Instead, they came in a ziplock plastic bag, and inside they each were in their own product box and the product boxes were a lot bigger than I expected! I honestly wasn’t sure what the heck they were at first! The outside of each box has a sticker with a number on it (01-06).

The liners were also a lot bigger than I expected! I was so surprised! The tubes with the color in them are pretty big, so you get a lot of product! The bottom of each one also has a sticker with a number on it (01-06), but there were 2 missing the stickers. Not a big deal to me. You can see the color of each through the tube, so I don’t need labels.

The applicator is a plastic point. They aren’t very flexible, so sometimes can be hard to work with. But, once you get used to them it’s easier. These ones do have a little give, which makes them a little easier. I never find it very easy to get a thin line with these. Usually they tend to kind of swipe the color, and not go as pigmented as when you use the side of the applicator. So, when I want a thin, precise line, I’ll usually put a decent amount onto my hand and dip a thin tipped brush in it. With some liners, you can’t do that because they dry down too fast. These ones give you time to work, so I like that. The thicker the amount, the longer it takes to dry down. So, if you put a thick amount in a little pile on your hand or a palette, you can easily dip your brush in and do your precise line before it dries down!

They are all beautiful and pigmented. The red, green, and brown seem more metallic than glittery to me. The gold like there’s gold glitter in it. The looks like it has silver glitter in it. The silver is the most glittery. It seems to have silver glitter in it.

They dry down completely. They don’t seem to get flakey or chunky.

Overall, I think this is a great set! You get 6 different colors. The part holding the product is huge, so you get a ton of product! You get a mix of metallic and glittery! They work well and are pigmented. They don’t get flakey. I definitely recommend!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Very cute, little dishes that can be used as dappen dishes or for other things!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
These are so cute! First, they’re heart shaped. Second, the glass has a rainbow look to it. Third, they’re small and most small things are cute!

They have a kind of felt on the bottom, which can keep it from scratching a surface if it slides, which is nice. But, it also means it slides easily. These are meant to be dappen dishes, so they are supposed to be used for liquids you’d use when doing your nails, such as slip solution, polish, etc. I found it had a habit of slipping easily when I dipped a brush in and wasn’t being careful about it (like if I dipped in and kind of hit the side). As long as I gently dipped into the dish, I didn’t have issues with it sliding, and even when it did slide it wasn’t a big deal because it’s not like it slid all the way across the table. Just something to be aware of.

The lids are clear, which I thought was interesting. I’m not sure why they don’t have the rainbow look like the bottom, but it doesn’t look bad with the clear lids. I love that these came with lids that actually fit. I previously saw dappen dishes I wanted, but they had these huge lids that just kind of sat on top of the dishes, so I didn’t get them. These lids actually fit the bottoms so I’m happy about that!

Even though these are meant to be dappen dishes, they can be used for many other things you might need a little container for. They’re very small, so there aren’t a ton of uses I can think of. But, they’d work for any kind of liquid or small items you’d want to put in them (like on your dresser to put your earrings and rings in when you take them off at the end of the night).

I think these are great dishes. The glass is thick and durable. They look beautiful. They’re cute. And you get 2 of them! I recommend!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: I think not all are natural, some are synthetic. Very soft hairs, but some shed A LOT at first
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
I thought it was really interesting that promoted the “sterility” of these brushes. They said, “Each makeup brush will undergo professional aseptic processing, Ensure that all users will not receive harm due to the product.” It said that “sterility - more assured.” They are in “food grade packaging” that is “sterile sealed packaging.” I’d never seen brushes promoted like that, so I was really interested to see it!

These come in a bubble mailer with the brushes inside and they are each individually sealed. They are each in the sealed sleeves that they show in the product photos. There’s even a paper insert. It says that the “Pro-18” brushes are “made of real animal hair, the handle is made of natural wood, will not shed hair, and is very soft. It is not easy to breed bacteria. Combination of 18 brushes, more professional.” It goes on to say that “his set of makeup brushes has been disinfected.” Finally, it says, “Because the hair density of makeup brush is relatively high, it is easy to breed bacteria in a humid environment. Please keep the makeup brush in a dry environment. When using the makeup brush, please use UV disinfection every 2-3 times (do not use high temperature disinfection to avoid damage to the hair). It is recommended to replace every 3-8 months.” I thought that last part was pretty interesting/odd. They are saying these are disinfected and that these are made of animal hair and “it is not easy to breed bacteria.” But, then it goes on to say that “because the hair density of makeup brush is relatively high, it is easy to breed bacteria in a humid environment.” So, apparently, they aren’t easy to breed bacteria, UNLESS they’re in a humid environment, in which case they will be easy to breed bacteria.

As I said, each brush is in its own sealed package. It’s kind of like a sealed ziplock bag, you rip off the top to reveal the ziplock part and open that to get to the brush. Most brush sets, the brushes come in individual plastic sleeves and you just pull the brush out of it. That can be annoying, but still be able to be done fairly quickly. This way is definitely a lot more annoying - having to rip each of the 18 packages open, then undo the ziplock, then take the brush out. It doesn’t take too much longer though. And, you end up with a lot more garbage with each of the packages. They didn’t have a chemical smell like some brush sets have. The product page said you can use them immediately, but I still washed mine first like I usually do with brushes.

I like natural hair brushes. I find that they apply my eyeshadow better. Natural haired brushes are good for powder products. Synthetic brushes are good for cream/liquid products.

I don’t like how the product page focuses so much on how the brushes are disinfected prior to getting to you and individually sealed, but they don’t provide much info on the brushes individually. They state that the brushes have wood handles. They don’t say what the ferrules are made out of. I’m pretty sure they’re plastic. They say that the hairs are animal hairs - horse hair. However, usually, when a brush is made of a specific type of hair, the brushes with that hair are the same color. These brushes have different colored hairs. For example, the 3 bigger brushes have black hairs, then some of the smaller brushes have brown hairs, and the flat paddle foundation brush is white with brown tips. So, it kind of makes me think they all are not animal hair - horse hair. It’s possible the black and brown hairs are both horse hair, but I can’t be sure. The flat paddle foundation brush I think is synthetic. It would make sense for it to be synthetic since it’s a foundation brush, and liquids work best with synthetic brushes. So, I don’t mind that. But, I wish they focused a little more on describing each brush and it’s hairs than they did on the brushes being sterile when they get to you.

I will say I almost didn’t get this set of brushes when I saw it said they were horse hair. I’ve had other cheaper brush sets before that had natural haired brushes, and the ones that were horse hair were always extremely soft and worked great, but shedded like CRAZY. So, I initially wasn’t going to get this set. But, they sounded like they were worth a try.

The brushes feel very lightweight, but durable. The handles are matte black with the brand name on them. There’s no other labels. The ferrules are silver.

You get 4 big brushes -
A large fan brush. This has black hairs. It’s very soft. I don’t get these brushes. For me, I only would ever use a fan brush to apply highlighter. I never like huge fan brushes like this one to apply my highlighter, so I never know what to do with them!

A fluffy powder/bronzer type brush. This has black hairs. It is very soft. The hairs seem to be cut evenly and I didn’t have any shedding so far.

An angled blush brush. This has black hairs. This one seemed to have uneven hairs. When I touched the hairs, a bunch started coming out. After a decent amount came out (see photos) I didn’t seem to have any more come out so far.

A flat paddle foundation brush. This seems to have synthetic hairs. Its silky like synthetic hairs can be. It’s soft. I never use flat paddle foundation brushes, but if you do use them, this one seems nice.

You get 14 smaller brushes
A fluffy angled brush. The hairs are black. This could be used for concealer, to powder under the eyes, etc. The hairs don’t seem cut very evenly (see photos, I tried to show it best I could). The brush is really soft, but with the hairs cut so unevenly, it makes me not really want to reach for it. But, I haven’t noticed any shedding.

A large shader brush. This has brown hairs. They’re really soft. This shed A LOT. When it kept shedding everywhere, I really worked the hairs and a lot came out but then it finally started to slow down. I haven’t noticed much since then, so hopefully it was just initially and it won’t shed anymore. I really hope it doesn’t shed much anymore because I do like it. It works great to put color in my crease and blend it out. With my small, hooded eyes, I need smaller brushes that are precise but I still need brushes to blend. This gets product where I want it and blends it out.

A medium shader brush. This has brown hairs. They’re really soft. This also shed A LOT. It was just like the large shader. I got out a ton of hairs and now I haven’t noticed much shedding, so hopefully it’s done with that! Like the larger shader brush, I really hope this doesn’t shed much anymore because I like it. Again, it’s smaller so it gets product right where I want it, but it’s still fluffy enough to blend out edges.

A fluffy kind of pencil brush. This has brown hairs. They’re really soft. I was really excited for this brush. I like pencil brushes for my small, hooded eyes. I really like them when they’re a little fluffy so I can use them to blend out small areas. This is perfect for that. Unfortunately, like the shader brushes, this shed A LOT, worse than the shader brushes. I think I got most of the hairs out that were shedding and haven’t noticed much since then, so hopefully it’s done with shedding because I really like it.

There’s 2 small shader brushes. They have brown hairs and are really soft. One is small and one is even smaller. They both shed a little but nowhere near as bad as the other ones I’ve mentioned so far. I like these to pack on color, put color on the outer corner, apply eyeshadow to my lower lash line, etc. They work great.

There’s a short kind of shader brush. It has brown hairs and is really soft. This would work good to apply product onto the lid, like a shimmer or metallic. It also works well to highlight the inner corner and brow bone.

There’s 3 other brushes that have brown hairs with dark brown or black tips. I think these are synthetic but I can’t be sure, but it would make sense for them to be synthetic. They’re all soft.
Angled brush. This works well for liner or brows. I like it for my brows because it’s really thin and can make great hair like strokes.
A flat brush. This works well for liner.
A tiny concealer type brush. I love this to use to cut my crease. Any brushes this size and shape are my go to brushes to cut my crease. I also like them to apply my inner corner highlight. They work well to use to spot conceal specific small areas too.

There’s 4 brushes left
A eyelash/brow comb/brush.
A smudging brush. This has like a hard sponge kind of tip. If you apply gel liner, you can use this to smudge it out really well. I don’t use brushes like this often because I feel they’re kind of harsh, tugging on the eye to smudge it out. But, it’s nice to have one or two for when I want to smudge out liner.
A thin eyeliner brush. This is really thin. It works well.
A spoolie. This is soft, not scratchy at all when brushing your brows out with it.

Overall, I think this is an okay brush set. Right now, I like it. I love how soft the hairs are. They work well. I really hated all the shedding I had with most of them, but since kind of working the hairs I seem to have gotten past that. As long as they don’t start shedding a lot again, I will really enjoy them and use them daily. If they start shedding a lot like they were initially, they’ll be going into the garbage! So, right now, I’d recommend them as long as you know they might have a shedding issue that might be able to be taken care of by kind of working the hairs to get those loose hairs out. I am going to continue using them and will update my review if they start shedding a lot again. So, right now, I’m giving them 3 stars. If they start shedding a lot again, I will come back and update my review and lower my rating. If they don’t start shedding a lot again, I will come back and update my review and increase my rating.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Works great to hold lashes with a thick enough line!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
First of all, I want to make it clear this is LINER GLUE - an eyeliner and lash glue in one. You get a clear one and a black one. Both are liner glue. I wanted to make that clear because I saw another review that said something about only expecting the tube with white liquid to be the glue and how it was stickier than the liner. I’m not sure what tube with white liquid the reviewer is talking about. Maybe the clear pen? Maybe this product page once had another product and the review is for that, which happens sometimes. I’m not sure. I just want to make it clear that BOTH the clear and black pens are eyeliner AND glue in 1.

They actually claim this is a 3-in-1 product - Eyeliner, lash glue, and eyelash serum. So, it claims you can use both pens as an eyeliner. You can use both pens as lash glue. And both pens are lash serums.

It wasn’t too long ago that I found out about 2-in-1 liner and glue pens. When I first found out about them, I thought they would be a gimmick and wouldn’t work, but they do...but not always. Like with any product, some work better than others. This one works well.

The caps - on the one hand they are on good and snug and won’t slip off, but on the other hand they are a pain to get off! You have to tug so hard that when it finally comes off you end up swiping the pen on your hand. That’s a pain! I’m hoping with time after removing the cap it’ll become looser and not so hard to remove!

The liner works well. The black is pigmented. It’s a little runny so it can bleed/feather. It stays put well. The clear is clear so I didn’t really try it as just a liner. If you’re using it just as a liner, it has a stickiness until it dries down completely, which doesn’t take long. If I’m just going to reach for eyeliner and not use false lashes, I wouldn’t really reach for this. I have liners I prefer over this one. It works nicely as the liner with your false lashes. I just wouldn’t really recommend it if you’re not going to use it with false lashes.

The glue part works well. If you shake it really well first, apply it immediately, apply a regular thickness line, and immediately apply your lash, the liner will hold your lashes really well and hold them all day. I say regular thickness line because with my small, hooded eyes, I tightline so my line is extremely thin. But, if you don’t tightline and do a regular line, the glue will hold well. But, if your line is too thin, the lashes will lift. If your eyes water at all, the lash will lift in that area. Luckily, you get a clear and a black one. The clear works well for me because I can do a thicker line and it dries clear so I don’t mind it! Unfortunately, the black one isn’t for me. If you like to tightline like I do, the clear will work well for you since it dries clear so it doesn’t matter if you do a thicker line than you normally would with your liner. If you do regular thickness liner, you would enjoy both the clear and the black!

As for the lash serum part of this 3-in-1 liner, I can’t really speak to that. It says that it has castor oil in the liners so they will help with growing thicker, longer lashes. I haven’t been using this long enough where I would notice something like that. Since I tightline, I am applying it right on my lash line. But, I’m not sure it’s getting applied on the lash line enough to work well as an eyelash serum. But, it’s nice that it could help. Better than a liner that doesn’t have castor oil and definitely wouldn’t help. So, I say it can’t hurt!

Overall, I think this is a nice lash liner glue. It works well as lash glue if you use a normal thickness line of liner. I like liner glue like these because they’re so much easier than applying lash glue, applying the lashes, and then applying an eyeliner. With a product like this, I apply it just like I would an eyeliner, and pop the lashes on top. It cuts down on the steps! For me, the clear works great since it dries clear so doing a thicker line of liner than I normally would isn’t a big deal. The black isn’t for me because I only like a tightline of liner being seen. But, if you tightline like me, the clear will work for you, and if you do normal liner, both will work for you!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: So cute!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This is so cute! I always wear claw clips like this, but they’re always just plain ones. I saw this and it looked like a cute way to dress up a claw clip but still be good for every day use!
