AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: So far seems to be working. NEED TO START ON CLEAN SHAVEN SKIN
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
So far I’m finding this easy to use and seeing some results.

I’ve never used a product like this before, so I started at the lowest setting. It doesn’t feel too hot at all. I felt a little something, like prickly or zapping, but it was very light and didn’t bother me or feel uncomfortable.

To use this, you shave and clean the surface hair FIRST. This says that it’s a “hair removal machine,” so it can seem confusing, like you can have hair and use this and it will remove the hair away AND inhibit it from growing back, but that isn’t how it says to use it. You’re supposed to start on a clean shaved area. Wear the glasses and turn it on to the level you want. You place the lighted part perpendicular to the skin.

For how often you use the machine, it states you can use it once every 2 days and adjust it based on your needs.

For results, it says many customers see good results in 6-12 weeks. It states that in the first few weeks you will still see some hair growth. At 8 weeks you will see a reduction in hair growth. It says that this is because many hairs may still not have been treated during their growth phase, so it’s important to continue weekly treatments with the machine. After 12 weeks, any remaining hair seen should be finer and lighter. You do continuous treatment every month as needed to help your skin permanently reduce the hair.

I have noticed it seems to work so far. I think it works better in areas where my hair isn’t as coarse. Like, on my upper legs, my hair is lighter and softer there. That makes sense because it did say that different hair types will have different hair removal speeds. It makes sense to me that the more coarse the hair is, the longer it would take to stop it from growing. I feel like this has slowed the growth of my hair. I’m interested to see if it stops it completely with continued use!

Overall, I think this is good machine. It’s easy to use. It is easy to hold and maneuver. It doesn’t hurt or get too hot. I have seen some results after just starting to use it. I’m hopeful I’ll continue seeing results. If you’re looking for something to stop your hair growth, I think this is worth a try.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Nice kit with all you need!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
You get everything you need in this kit!

There’s 8 tubes of poly gel. They each are individually sealed in plastic wrapping. They state that the colors you get are - “White,” “transparent,” “apricot,” “orange,” “gray,” “transparent pink,” “pink,” and “sequined glitter.” These are basically the colors you get, but I would describe a couple of the colors differently. To me, there is a peach and a peachy pink color. I’m not sure which one they’re calling apricot and which one they’re calling orange. It really doesn’t matter. What they call “gray” I would call more of a brown nude color. They also call one a transparent pink and one a pink. Again, not sure which one they refer to as which, but that doesn’t matter. I would call one a kind of purplish-pink (like a lilac pink mix) and the other a pink.

There’s a bottle of slip solution. I like that one is included. A lot of kits like these don’t include a slip solution. But, I also use isopropyl alcohol as a slip solution, so it’s not a big deal to me when one isn’t included.

You get a dual sided tool - brush on one end, spatula on the other. You also get a pair of tweezers and a nail file.

There’s 2 bottles of top coat and a bottle of base coat.

You get nail forms assorted in sizes. They are separated in a plastic packaging that has a clear plastic cover. It’s just thin packaging. I would have liked them to be in something sturdier, but it works.

You get some nail art items - a little circular plastic piece that has sections divided with small different colored rhinestones in them, 5 different rolls of stripping tape, and 6 small jars of different glitters.

Finally, you get a mini UV/LED nail lamp that comes with a USB cable. Mini lamps are never very powerful. For gel polish? I find that they get the job done but I usually have to do it a couple times. Even if my polish says cure for 30 seconds with an LED lamp and 30 seconds is usually long enough with my regular UV/LED lamp, with mini lamps like this I’ll usually have to hit again for another 30 seconds. If I do VERY thin layers and hold the lamp as close to my nails as possible, I can usually get away with doing one 30 second cycle. But, for poly gels these mini lamps aren’t the greatest. They take a while to cure it. Again, it will get the job done, but you’ll need to be patient. Personally, I’ll usually just use my regular full sized lamp. But, anyone who is new to using nail products that require curing with an LED/UV lamp and doesn’t own a regular full sized one, this would get the job done.

Overall, I think this is a great set. It has everything you need including a lamp and a slip solution. There’s a good assortment of colors. The poly gels work well. I think this would work great for anyone who loves doing poly gels or for someone just starting off!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Great mask! Helped decrease size of my breakouts and lessen redness!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
I’ve tried 111skin products before and enjoyed them, so when I saw this mask I was excited to try it.

I get hormonal breakouts on my chin area and around my mouth. I thought by 35 I’d be done having to deal with breakouts, but nope. So, I’m always looking for something that is helpful to my skin and breakouts. When I saw this was a mask for blemish prone skin, I was even more excited to try it!

This has 2 separate parts - top half and bottom half. The top half is meant to help control oil and shine without messing with moisture in the area. The bottom half is meant to combat lower face eruptions and calm skin. That was perfect for me since my breakouts are always around my mouth and on my chin!

I’ve had masks before that came in 2 separate parts, but never that has each part targeting something different. Another thing I thought was unique was that these were packaged separately. It seemed as though they were together in the standard mask packaging. But, they were actually separate packaging but just together, when you can separate the package into 2 separate halves. I thought that was really unique so if you wanted, you could do them at separate times. Of course, the top half has 2 eye holes and the bottom half has 1 mouth hole. So, they aren’t made to be used on whatever half of your face you want. But, it’s nice you can use them at separate times if you wanted. Like, if I’m breaking out on my lower half but don’t feel the need for oil control on the top half, I can just use the bottom mask and save the top mask for when I do want oil control. So, I think that’s nice.

111Skin products are pretty pricey for me, and this mask is no differ. It’s $32 (at the time of writing this review), which, to me, is CRAZY expensive for ONE mask. Even though it comes as 2 halves, it’s still really one mask. So, $32 is a lot in my opinion. But, if it works well enough, I wouldn’t mind splurging on myself once in a while to get it.

I do feel like the mask works well. The top half didn’t dry my skin out at all, but did help with oiliness. The bottom half helped lessen the 2 pimples I had - they decreased in size by the next day and weren’t as red.

Overall, I think this is a really nice mask. The only downside I found is that it’s $32 for a single mask! That’s pricey! It works really well though. So, it will definitely be something I’d be willing to splurge on once in a while to treat myself or if I feel I really need it! If you’re able to spend it or willing to splurge for it, I recommend it!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Gives light coverage that evens out skin, can be built up. Hydrating and smooth
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
These come with 3 product boxes wrapped with plastic around them holding them together. All 3 of the outer product boxes look exactly the same, so initially I thought they had sent me the wrong thing - 3 foundations - instead of 2 foundations with sponges. But, once I took off the plastic wrapping and felt the 3 boxes, I could tell that 1 had sponges in it. Kind of weird they put them inside one of their foundation boxes. Not sure how comfortable I am with them not being wrapped on their own, but rather handled someone and placed into a foundation box? But, I guess either a machine or person normally handles makeup sponges in order to get them in their packaging, so this isn’t that weird 🤷‍♀️ Then, I took the sponges out and they looked like they had lint/paper or something all over them. I always wash my sponges before use anyways, and these felt soft and bouncy, so I figured I’d give them a try once I washed them. They worked really well so I’m glad I didn’t toss them right away. They are really soft and bouncy and increase in size once wet. Even though I really like them, I took a star off for them coming in a foundation box and having paper/lint all over them.

This comes in a thick frosted glass bottle with a dropper to dispense. It’s a nice clean way of dispensing product and to be able to control the amount of product you get out, which I like.

It claims to be made from natural ingredients. The ingredients are listed here on the product page and on the box. I put them at the end of this review. There were some ingredients that were listed oddly. When I first saw them listed I didn’t recognize them, so I looked them up. I’m not sure if they had to be translated and they got messed up that way or what, but they just weren’t written completely correct. Like I said, I put the ingredients at the end of my review. First, I put them exactly how they’re listed on the product page and the box. Then, below that, I wrote out what ingredients I felt were written the wrong way and wrote out what they should have been written as. If you want to look them up, it definitely makes it easier looking them up written the right way, at least for me it did. The ingredients can come from natural things. It does include parabens (methylparaben and propylparaben). I know a lot of people now are against parabens and now a lot of companies are producing “paraben free” products, but parabens are used preservatives. If they aren’t using parabens, which have been used regularly in products for many years, for the preservatives, they’re going to be using something else. Methylparaben occurs naturally in a handful of fruits (like blueberries), but it can also be created synthetically. Propylparaben is also a natural substance found in many plants and some insects.

I had gotten another foundation from Amazon that came in a glass bottle with a dropper to dispense similar to this one. I got that one in the lightest shade and it ended up being way too warm for me. I got this one in #2 because looking at the swatches it seemed lighter than #1. #1 seemed darker and warmer than #2 and #3. #2 and #3 seemed to be the lightest shades, with #2 looking more pink and #3 more yellow. I decided to go with #2. I always hate when companies make their #1 shade darker than the ones that come after it! I never understand that! But, I’m glad they had swatches to look at!

#2 is light enough for me, and like it seemed in the product photo of swatches, it has a pink tone to it. I did a swatch comparing this foundation in #2 to Maybelline Fit Me Matte+Poreless in 110 Porecelain. As you can tell, Maybelline one is more warm toned and this foundation is more cool toned.

It gives a nice natural, slightly dewy finish. It gives okay coverage. One thin layer just evens out my skin tone, but you can build it up some and/or use a brush instead of a sponge and get more application. With a foundation like this, that is a thinner consistency, if you want the most amount of coverage you can get from it, I recommend using a short haired, dense foundation brush. If you want to blend it seamlessly into the skin where it just evens out skin tone, you can use a sponge or use a fluffier brush to blend it onto the skin (I like using a fluffy dual fiber brush or my luxie 522 brush - it’s called a tapered highlighting brush, but I love the look it gives when I use it to blend in a thin consistency foundation! It just looks so seamless!). I usually don’t powder my face completely, only where I absolutely need to. But, with this foundation, I definitely recommend powdering! If I do a thin layer and powder, I don’t get much transfer at all.

Overall, I think it’s an okay foundation. If you like a natural but dewy finish, like a foundation that you can even out your skin tone with or build it up for a little more coverage, and don’t mind that you have to powder it to keep the transfer down, this would work for you. Personally for me, I like how hydrating this feels. It doesn’t cling to dry patches at all. Where a lot of foundations, even dewy ones, will sometimes look dry or cakey (like between my eyebrows, no matter how hard I try I can’t get foundation to look smooth and good there 😠), this one doesn’t do that! It looks nice and smooth there! I like using it on days where I just need to even out my skin.

INGREDIENTS
AS LISTED ON BOX AND ON AMAZON PRODUCT PAGE
Water, glycerin, propylene glycol, poly two methyl siloxane ring five, titanium dioxide, palmitic acid ethyl ester, liquid paraffin, PEG-30 two poly hydroxy stearic acid ester, poly two methyl siloxane cross-linked polymer, petrolatum, C12-15 alcohol benzoate, magnesium sulfate, avocado fruit fat, beeswax, rose flower extract, lanolin, magnesium stearate, polysorbate -80, methylparaben and propylparaben, phenoxyethanol ethylhexylglycerin, rose oil, iron oxides.

MY CHANGE OF HOW SOME INGREDIENTS ARE LISTED
“Poly two methyl siloxane ring five” - Cyclopentasiloxane D5 (Cyclo = ring, penta = 5, dimethyl = 2 methyls)
“PEG-30 Two Poly Hydroxy Stearic Acid Ester” - PEG-30 Dipolyhydroxystearate (di = 2, stearate = salt or ester of stearic acid)
“Poly Two Methyl Siloxane Cross-Linked Polymer” - Polydimethylsiloxane
“C12-15 Alcohol Benzoate” - I think it means C12-15 Alkyl benzoate

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Very finely milled! Doesn’t look like have powder on!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
Overall, I think this is a great powder! I love how finely milled it is! It’s so soft and velvety on the skin! It doesn’t look like I have powder on, but sets my makeup in place. It looks and feels nice on the skin. You get a good amount of product. I’m really happy with it! The only thing I don’t like is how hard the lid is to twist initially. I also don’t like the product page talking about natural ingredients - baichi flower seed oil and jojoba seed oil - being in the powder and that not being on the ingredient list. So, I took a star off for that. But, other than that, I recommend this powder. If like me, you don’t usually like powders and the only ones you do like are finely milled, you’ll love this powder! If you’ve had trouble finding powders that work for you. If they tend to make your skin look dry, powdery, or cakey. I recommend trying this one out!

This comes in an outer product box. It is made in China. It has a cruelty free logo (PETA). The ingredients are listed on the back. It includes mica and parabens.

It’s odd because the product page states that it’s made of “natural safe ingredients” and has “baichi flower seed oil water-oil balance, long-lasting makeup” and “jojoba seed oil moisturize the skin,” but neither of those ingredients are found in the ingredient list on the back of the product box. So, I don’t understand where that comes from? I hate when there’s what seems like blatantly false claims on a product page. It makes me not trust anything from the brand.

The jar of powder is square. It’s a good size. It is plastic. The bottom is clear but frosted and matte. The top has the same design as the front of the box. It has a nice look to it.

I hate to say it, but how to get the top off had me a little confused at first 🙈 I initially thought it would twist off, but when I went to twist it, it didn’t seem to want to move. Then, I thought, well since it’s square, maybe it will pull off. So, I carefully tried to pull the top off, but it didn’t want to budge. Then, I tried twisting it again, this time really putting effort into it and it finally moved and I got it off. At first it seemed like it only went halfway, but wouldn’t twist any more (again, I was being careful because I didn’t want powder getting everywhere). Then, I just lifted it up and it came off. I thought after the first time it would be easier to get the top off, but it wasn’t. You still really need to put some elbow grease into it every single time, which is annoying. If you have trouble with things like that, this might not be the powder for you. There was a clear sticker covering the holes, which I always appreciate! So, had I yanked the top off, Powder wouldn’t have gotten everywhere! But, you never know since some brands don’t do that! But, I’m glad this one did!

Another thing, I kind of wish the part with the holes, where the powder is, I wish it was square like the jar. I always dump powder into the lid and dip my brush into that. Then, whatever powder I have left, I dump back into the jar. Usually, I can just take the cap with the leftover powder and carefully put it on and the powder will fall into the main part. With this, if I do that the powder gets down on the edges of the jar (see photos), so I always have to make sure to carefully dump the powder back in before putting the lid on.

I had a hard time deciding which shade I wanted to get. Usually, I go with translucent. But, sometimes I like a little extra coverage from a skin toned powder. But, this powder had an option for a pink powder, and I always heard pink was good for brightening, so then I thought about that one! The descriptions on the middle of the product page didn’t really help. For #1, “Ivory White,” it said, “Suitable for fair skin. Create white makeup.” I was initially thinking this one was translucent, until I read the description. I’m fair skinned, but I don’t know what they mean by white makeup. But, it seemed like it was going to have a white tint to it, which I didn’t want. For #2, “Natural Color” they had, “Suitable for any race. Create light makeup.” If it’s “suitable for any race” that would imply it’s translucent, but it didn’t look translucent. It looked like a fair skin toned color. For #3, “Soft Pink,” it had, “Suitable for pink skin. Create a glossy, ruddy makeup.” I have fair skin and I’m cool toned, so pink skin makes sense. Glossy doesn’t seem too bad, but I’m not sure what they meant by that. Do they mean it’s going to give a glow? And who wants ruddy makeup? See how confused I was! 🤦‍♀️

I thought I ended up going with #2 “Natural Color,” and the box mine came in had “#2” on the top flap, but when I looked at the color of the powder through the frosted clear bottom it looked soft pink. When I first dumped some out into the lid it looked soft pink. But, when I swatched it, it seemed more of a fair skin toned color. So, I THINK I got the right shade (#2 Natural Color). It definitely works for my fair skin. But, I don’t see how this would be “suitable for any race.” To me, it seems like it blends out MOSTLY transparent. But, it does seem like there might be a HINT of fair shade/white to it, so I’m not sure if it will work for medium to darker skin tones.

The powder is very finely milled. It has almost a velvety feel when you touch it. I am 35, have normal to dry skin with some extremely dry areas, and suffer from hormonal acne. In my experience, most powders make my skin look dry or powdery or cakey, so I only like using powder in specific places where I absolutely need it. Even then, there’s only a handful of powders I like for that purpose that look good on my skin. This has become one of those! Out of the handful of powders I like on my skin, the one thing they all have in common is that they are all VERY finely milled. I find that the more fine the powder is, the less it looks like you have powder on your face. It just sets my makeup in place in my oily areas without making it look dry/powdery/cakey.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Beautiful liquid duo chrome glitter shadow!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
[[VIDEOID:2a72e8985c923c5323e75483ce8ba7f0]] I have become a HUGE fan of the Mynena brand! I first tried their loose pigment duo chrome eyeshadows and loved them and have been trying different products ever since and they haven’t disappointed me yet!

This comes in a white outer product box. It is made in the PRC. It has cruelty free logo (PETA logo). The ingredients are listed on the box.

Inside the box, the tube is sealed with plastic wrapper. The tube is a nice size. The top is white. The bottom of the tube is clear so you can see the color through it. The brand name is written in gold. It’s simple but cute.

I got the shade “Ashley.” I had trouble deciding which one I wanted when I was picking it out. Well, I knew which one I wanted, but the product photos showing the swatches didn’t have them labeled. At the time I chose mine, the first product photo as of just the tube (no eye showing the color on the lid), and the other photos were the swatches on the arms. Now, the swatches on the arms still aren’t labeled, but they have the eye with the product on it together with the tube in the first product photo, then they have additional photos of eyes wearing the product. I like that they added those. Now, you can tell which one it is that you want in order to select the correct one. Before, with just the swatches and tubes, you could easily tell that the blue one was “Roxanna,” “Valeria” seemed to be the orange colored one, and “”Fio” seemed to be the green gold one. But, but aside from that it seemed you could easily mix up the others. Like, “Valeria” seemed like the orange colored one. But, “Ashley” and “Eiliana” tubes looked the same to me - just white product inside the tube - so it was hard to really tell the difference from the photos and unlabeled swatches. I wanted the one with the pink in it, so I went with “Ashley.” Luckily, I guessed right. Now that the photos are on the product page showing each color on the eyes, it’ll be a lot easier for people to choose the color they want and be sure they’re getting the one they want. So I like that they changed it!

The product photo makes it look like it’s white with a light pink shift. In person looking at it through the tube, it looks like there’s white, silver, light pink in it, and even a hint of gold.

The applicator is a doe foot applicator. It’s flat on each side and rounded at the tip. It works great applying product to the eyes.

I did swatches on my clean forearm (no lotion, primer, etc.). I did 2 sets. The first set is 1 layer. The top is 1 swipe. I took the applicator out of the tube and did 1 swipe straight across my arm. Then, below that, I took what was left on the applicator and swiped it a few times to make an even layer and I flipped the applicator over to get the product off the other side too. The second set is 2 layers. I did the same thing as I did in the first set, except I just did it on top of the first set. The top I did a second swipe over the initial one. I took the applicator out of the tube and did 1 swipe right over the swipe I did in the first set. Then, below that, I took what was left on the applicator and swiped it over top of the initial one to make an even layer and flipped the applicator over to get the product off that side too. I took photos, which I labeled, and did a video of both sets (labeled those too). In the second set, I also made sure to get a lot of product on the applicator and then just kind of did a little blob above the 2 swatches. I was hoping it would show the mix of white, silver, and light pink well.

The formula is really nice. A lot of times with liquid eyeshadows, especially glittery ones, when you’re applying it, if you try to go over an area that already has product while it’s still wet, it will pick up product and make an uneven layer. With this formula, it doesn’t do that. It lays it down nicely and doesn’t pick up product if you go over the same area again. I really like that! It also layers nicely! It dries down quick, but you have time to work with it before it does. It is glittery but once it dries down completely, the glitter doesn’t transfer and doesn’t fall off all over your face throughout the day.

Overall, I think it’s a beautiful duo chrome liquid glitter eyeshadow! It has a beautiful duo chrome shift to it! You get a decent sized tube. The tube looks nice. The liquid eyeshadow has a nice formula that applies easily and looks nice. It looks nice with 1 layer, but builds up well if you want more. It stays in place all day without transferring or glitter falling all over your face all day. It’s definitely high in price for a liquid glitter eyeshadow. BUT, its a duo chrome. I’ve found any time a product is a duo/multi chrome, it costs more than just a solid color. Most tubes of liquid eyeshadow with a nice formula like this are close in price, usually a little less, depending on the brand. So, for this to be duo chrome, I don’t think it’s overly priced. If you’re looking for a beautiful duo chrome liquid glitter shadow, I’d recommend this!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Exactly what I needed to make picking up rhinestones/gems/sequins/etc. easy!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
These are great! They feel nice to hold. Not flimsy. They’re comfortable in the hand. Plus, they have a cute look to them!

They are dual ended. You have the wax tip that picks up rhinestones/gems or any other nail art like sequins or charms. Then there is a stainless steel tip that you use to press down the rhinestone/gem/etc. to keep them in place. You can also pick up a little rhinestone glue with the stainless steel tip and use it to apply a small dot of glue to where you want it on the nail. It’s so helpful!

I needed something to help me pick up rhinestones, gems, sequins, charms, etc. When I tried to use one of those pencils to pick up rhinestones, it worked but not every time, so I’d have to fuss around with it. Using tweezers worked, but it’s hard to not have the rhinestones/gems slip through them and sequins are so thin it’s hard to pick up just one. I tried using a little brush to pick up sequins and things like that, which worked, but sometimes I’d only get 1 or 2, sometimes I’d get a ton that were overlapping. So nothing seemed to work right and be totally easy to use. Until these! I really have no complaints!

Overall, I definitely recommend these if you do a lot of nail rhinestones/gems or art using sequins/charms/etc. It’s totally worth it to help with the ease of application and save you time and frustration trying to use something else. If you don’t do a lot of nail art using stuff like rhinestones/gems/sequins/charms/etc., then it might be fine just using something you probably already have like tweezers or a brush. But, if you were going to buy one of those pencils that pick up rhinestones/gems, I say skip that and go for these! They work so much better and you get 2 of them!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Powder gives light wash of color. Good for someone who doesn’t need too much.
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
A little while back I got an eyebrow stamp kit like this and loved it! The only thing I wished was that the eyebrow stamp was a little thinner. When I saw this kit and saw the stamp looked a lot thinner than the one I had, I had to try it!

This comes with the brow stamp, 24 brow stencils, and 4 spoolie brushes.

Theres a whopping 24 eyebrow stencils included in this kit! That’s crazy! So, I’m sure most everyone can find a shape that they like for their brows among these stencils. Unlike most kits that have brow stencils like these, these have adhesive backing that sticks to you. Most kits I’ve gotten like these the stencils are plastic, so reusable. I like that they stick because you don’t have to worry about holding them perfectly in place while also trying to use the stamp to fill in your brows and worry about it moving some. But, I don’t like that they aren’t really reusable like this since once you pull off the backing and stick them on, they won’t stick anymore.

The first time I tried a brow powder stamping kit I wasn’t expecting much. I kind of expected this to make ugly, thick, blocky looking eyebrows. But, this actually works great! The product in the stamp is powder, so it creates a nice, light color, and you can dab more to build it up if you want. Once you use the spoolie, it looks pretty natural. You can also add pencil to if you wanted.

I don’t have thick brows, but I don’t have extremely sparse brows. My brows are thinner, where you can see skin poking through, but there’s basically an even amount of hair all the way across. I used to just leave my brows be, but when I do a full face of makeup I do feel like my brows need a little something. So, I started doing my brows. I usually do a little tinted brow gel. It usually gives enough tint to make them look a little fuller and complete, but not so much where they look too thick. I feel like since I’m just starting to do my brows, whenever I have them filled completely I think they look too thick and weird 😂 So, I like a middle area. So, using this stamp works well for me. If I’m doing full glam, I like to apply it to get a kind of light wash of color. Then, I’ll kind of go over the tail a little with some more powder to darken it a little more. Then, I’ll take a brow pencil and do a few kind of hair like strokes in the front. Sometimes I’ll go in and do some brow gel if I feel they need more defined. This fills them out nicely, makes them look complete, but doesn’t make them look too dark or full. If I am doing a more natural look, I’ll just use the brow powder in the stamp. I do feel that there isn’t a ton of product that comes out and I’m not sure how much product is in the stamp. I don’t mind that not a lot comes out, I actually prefer it. But, if you wanted more product, it might be kind of annoying for you.

Overall, I think this is a nice little set! It is a nice way to try different brow shapes to see what you like for yourself. The product works well. The brow powder looks natural and lasts nicely in the brows. I would definitely recommend this for someone who isn’t sure about their brow shape - what they like best on their face, what shape works best, how to fill in brows, etc. This set will help with those things! If you’re someone that just likes a little wash of color and fuller, more filled out brows, this would help with that. If you’re someone who likes a lot of color in the brows, you might not like this since it just gives a wash of color. So, I would recommend it but only if you’re someone who wants to try out different brow shapes to get an idea of what works for you or if you’re someone who likes a light wash of color throughout their brows.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Nice small but angled tip. Little dry so need to press a little harder, but stays put well
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
I usually like micro brow pencils with really small pointed tips rather than angled tips. Usually angled tips are thicker than I like, but I do like how quickly they fill brows. This is the perfect combo of both you get a thin, precise tip that’s angled. I feel like the formula is drier than I usually like. I usually go for creamier brow pencils, but I like the tip and as long as you press a little harder it works well. It also stays in place really well.

Overall, I think this is a really nice brow pencil. If you’re like me and usually like the micro brow pencils but like how quick angled tips fill in the brows, I think you’d like this if you don’t mind that it isn’t creamy and you need to press a little harder.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Fills in fine lines and pores giving a smooth base for foundation
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This is interesting! I’ve never seen a primer that comes with a brush built in like this! You push the bottom and 3 dots come out onto the brush. How I apply my primer usually depends on the primer I use. There’s some I use that I apply with my fingers to help melt the product into my skin and really press it into my skin. There’s some I apply with a brush to really spread it out. A while ago I watched a video from a well known makeup artist. He said that if you want to hide your pores, you can use a brush and basically press the product INTO the pores. Yes, your occluding the pore by using the bristles on the brush to put product INTO the pores, rather than just going over the pores, but if you wash your face well at the end of the day it shouldn’t be an issue. He said when you take the brush, you use the bristles to push the product into the pores, which fills them, and leads to an even base. If you use a product that just kind of layers over the pores, they aren’t filled, they just have a layer over them. A lot of times just having a layer over them works. It creates a smooth layer to put your base on. But, throughout the day the layer kind of breaks down and you end up with your pores showing. If you had actually put product into the pores, then they would continue to be filled and leave you looking smooth all day. So, ever since then I try to use a brush when applying product where I want my pores filled. So, this coming with a built in brush was perfect!

The brush is soft. It isn’t rough or scratchy. With 1 push giving 3 dots of product onto the brush I have enough product for everywhere I want to use it.

It makes my skin nice and smooth, so I have a smooth base to apply my foundation on.

Overall, I think this is a great primer! It fills in fine lines and pores. The built in brush really helps with that. And foundation goes over it great!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Luckily, I got the full nails as shown in product photos, not just tips!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
These come in a nice little box with the sizes assorted into little compartments. The box has a latch closure that is easy to open and close.

I saw another review that stated that they thought these were more press on nails even though the description said nail tips and that she can’t use them because what she got were actual nail tips, not what the product photos showed. That surprised me because I got what the product photos show. I’m glad I did because, like the other reviewer, I didn’t want tips. Even though the title says “nail tips.” The description says, “square full cover square nail tips” and the product photos show full nails, not tips. When you scroll down to the lower part of the product page, where it has “Product Description,” it states, “Shape: Full Cover.” So, even though they say “nail tips,” their product photos and descriptions imply they are full nails. So, like the other reviewer, I was hoping for full nails. Unlike the other reviewer, I did get full nails like what are shown in the product photos. So, I’m really happy about that! Another reviewer who provided photos also got the ones that I did, which are the same ones shown in the product photos. So, I’m not sure why the other reviewer got different ones. But, the company should really figure that out so that customers get what is shown in the product photos!

Anyways, the nails are nice. They’re thinner, but not too thin. They are solid white and really shiny. The product page has “recommendations for use,” which states, “Lady french acrylic style artificial false nails have a smooth surface. It is recommended to polish the surface to make it adherent.” I definitely agree with that. They are so smooth and shiny, if you want it to adhere good, you want to file the inside some to get them to stick the best and adhere for the longest. If I didn’t do that, they lifted pretty quickly. But, as long as I did that, they lasted a long time!

I expected these to be a little shorter than they were, like just over my nail beds. But, they were longer than that. I’d rather have them longer than I need and just cut and file them, so I didn’t mind. They’re still definitely short compared to most nails.

Overall, these are great! They are full nails, not just tips (at least the ones I got, which are the ones shown in the product photos). You get a nice assortment of sizes in a nice container. They are solid white. They adhere well to the nail bed when you file the inside down a little first. They hold polish well and last really well as long as you file the inside down before gluing them. I recommend!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Beautiful except for hair along headband
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This comes in a black box. Inside the wig is in netting. There’s a wig cap and an additional headband. The product page stated that you would get 2 random headbands included, but I just got the one.

I love headband wigs because they’re so easy! You don’t have to glue or tape anything. You just throw it on and boom, you’re done!

This has a nice black headband. You can put on any headband you want over it to switch up the style and to make it go with your mood/outfit! Like I said before, the product page states that it comes with 2, but I only got 1 with mine.

The hair is extremely soft. You can easily run your fingers through it. It doesn’t tangle at all and I didn’t have any issues with shedding. It looked beautiful right out of the box. However, the line of hair near the headband doesn’t look that great. You can see the cap underneath along the edge of the headband it and it just doesn’t look great. Luckily, you can put another headband over it, like the one included, and that covers that area so you can’t see it. I also don’t like that the hairs along that area are extremely short. They’re mixed in with the longer ones, but you can see the shorter ones. Again, once I put another headband on over the black one, I didn’t notice it. But, I’ve gotten other headband wigs here on Amazon for around the same price, and they looked better along the hairline of the headband.

Overall, the wig is pretty. The hair is gorgeous. I just don’t like a the hairline along the headband. Since you can still wear it and not notice that when you put another headband over it, I’m just taking 1 star off.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Stunning!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This comes packaged nicely. It comes in an outer product box. It has styrofoam protecting it well. It even had a little styrofoam kind of eye mask protecting the eyes! Mine did have a little gouge on the collarbone, but it was only little so not a big deal to me.

It’s GORGEOUS! She has makeup and beautiful eyes with lashes! There’s a kind of wig cap on top of the head that seems to be glued on.

It doesn’t state the size of the head or how tall the mannequin is. The head seems to fit standard wigs (22-22.5”). There is a photo that shows a measuring tape around the head. Why they could show that but not actually state the measurement is beyond me. But, it looks like it’s about 54 and 1/4 cm. 54 cm is 21 inches, which seems about right. When I put a 22” wig on this, it fits snugly. I measured the height and it’s about 16.5” tall.

The bottom has a kind of felt on it so it moves easily.

She even has pierced ears if you want to put earrings in.

Overall, this is a gorgeous, well made mannequin head! You can use it for wigs and jewelry.

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Beautiful! But unfortunately DRIES OUT IN A COUPLE MONTHS!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
[[VIDEOID:aef92a6ecb4755ec5636ddbdac7d2be]] 🔴UPDATE: I am updating my review because after having this for a few months, it has turned into a multichrome rock 😒 I have had it for about 5 months now and I have always kept the seal on it and kept the cap on tight after using it. I went to use it after not having used it for a month and found it completely dried up. It’s literally solid rock. I tried rewarming it, adding oil, and other things I’ve done for dried out gel pots and cream eyeshadows in the past but none of that worked for this. I had a video showing the shifts of this. But, you can only have 1 video and I thought showing how it turns into a rock was more important 😂 It’s a shame because it worked so well and was so beautiful. At first I thought $18.99 for this jar wasn’t bad at all because it only takes a little bit so it would last for a loooong time. But, since it dries out so quick, $18.99 is pretty darn pricey! Unless you’re going to use it every single day for the first few months, and even then I don’t see you using all the product up. I’m even more upset because I did get a second pot of this not long ago, so now I know what the future holds for that one. Such a shame. Unfortunately, I have to change my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I decided to give 2 instead of 1 because it works amazing when it’s not dried up.

🔴ORIGINAL REVIEW
This comes in an outer product box. The ingredients are listed on the side. It is made in China. The product page says it is smudge proof, paraben free, vegan, and cruelty free. I didn’t see anything on the packaging saying anything about being cruelty free or logos. But, that doesn’t mean it isn’t.

For use it says, “Take a tiny amount of Shadow Potion with a flat brush. Apply to the desired area with light pressure.” I’m not sure what “Shadow Potion.” It kind of sounds like something you mix this with, but it doesn’t say anything about mixing, so it’s more like these are called “Shadow Potion.” But, the product info just calls them Multichrome Eyeshadow. There’s nothing calling them “Shadow Potion” except for when it’s talking about how to use it.

It comes in a plastic jar. The lid screws off. There is a plastic seal with a little tab to use to pull it up. I love that! A lot of products like this I get will have tinfoil seals that you’re supposed to just take off and throw out, but then the product has a chance of drying out. So, I love this has the plastic cover so that it helps keep it from drying out! The jar isn’t filled up. The product page says that the item weighs 3 grams. I’m guessing that’s how much the product weighs, not the actual jar with the product in it. But, it would be nice if the jar was filled a little more, especially at $17.99 (price at time of review).

I got the shade “Nebula.” In the the jar (in product photos and in person), it looks like it’s reddish purple with green and gold. But, then the product photo of the swatches has it looking like a lighter purple and greenish gold. So I was really excited to try it out and see what it looked like!

In person I don’t see what the swatch photo shows exactly. It’s more like what it looks like in the jar - a maroonish purple, shifting to a darker brighter purple, and green to goldish green. It’s really pretty, so I don’t mind it. The last photo that has swatches has more realistic ones. I’m not sure why they chose to put the other swatch photo before that one. Really, the first swatch photo shouldn’t even be included since it’s not realistic, at least for the “Nebula” shade.

I did a video showing swatches of them. I showed it on my finger after application. Then I show the swatches in direct indoor lighting. Then I show the swatches in indirect natural lighting (window in back).

It’s a cream so it glides on easily. It takes a minute to dry down but then it’s set in place and doesn’t move. It can crease if you have oily lids, but if you use a glitter glue or an eyeshadow primer I found it helps a lot.

Overall, I think this is beautiful! It seems a little pricey, but a little goes a LONG way so it should last a long time, and most times multichromes like this are expensive, especially cream ones. So, I think it’s a decent price. It works great. It is easy to apply, sets down and stays put. I recommend!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Great smooth, silky powder that doesn’t make skin feel dry!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text: This comes in a nice little black compact with a mirror in the lid. It’s a very smooth, silky powder. It glides onto the skin without looking powdery. I have normal to dry skin, more on the dry side, with some extremely dry areas. This doesn’t accentuate the dryness at all. It makes my skin look nice and smooth and sets my makeup nicely without making my skin feel dry. It doesn’t really provide much coverage, but it does slightly add to coverage I already have from my foundation and concealer. At $9.99, I think it’s an amazing powder!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Great white eyeliners for lower waterline!
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text: These are great! They come in a box all together, not individually. They each have caps. They are sharp. They are the kind of pencils you need to sharpen on your own. They work well in the lower waterline, which is where I use my white eyeliners. A lot of white liners go on great but fade away quickly. These last well in the waterline. They are pigmented, but not so much so where it’s stark white, which I don’t mind since I have such dark brown, almost black, eyes. If a white liner is really pigmented, it can look a little too much. So, these work great! Plus, you get 12 so it’s a great value I think!

AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_title: Nice glowy finish with good coverage. Contains chemical sunscreen ingredients
AEMP3A7IKW37CMWFXNKXWW6HGJHA_1.review_text:
This comes in an outer product box. It is made in Korea. The info on the box is not in English. I assume it’s Korean since that’s where it’s made. I hate when companies sell a product in the US, but then don’t put the product info in English. They did include the ingredients on the product page, I included them at the end of the review. This is NOT reef safe since it contains chemical sunscreen ingredients like octinoxate and octocrylene. I didn’t realize this had chemical sunscreen ingredients in it like octinoxate, octisalate, and octocrylene. I prefer physical sunscreens. But, it was my own fault for not looking closer at the ingredient list before getting this.

This does contain silicones, alcohol, and parfum too.

It has some good ingredients too like niacinamide, glycerin, jojoba seed oil, adenosine, sunflower seed oil, squalane, centella asiatica leaf extract, ascorbic acid (vitamin C), honey extract, and madecassoside.

I love cushion foundations. I have normal to dry skin, more on the dry side, with some extremely dry areas. Cushion foundations usually give me great coverage but look natural and healthy on my skin. This one claimed to “plump your skin” with “advanced luminous lasting cushion.” It claimed to be “fitting and superstay” that it had “advanced formula Fixative Polymer technology, which forming a moisture film on your skin, keep your skin hydrated, moistured and leaving your skin with the most luminous look. Simultaneously, this film helps to keep the foundation layer thin yet stay fit all day long.” I didn’t like the idea of a film on my skin, but liked the idea of it hydrating my skin and giving it a luminous look, but lasting all day.

This comes in a black plastic compact. It has magnetic closure. When you open the top there is a mirror in the lid and a little cushion applicator. When you take off the cushion applicator you’ll see the little plastic shelf that covers the cushion foundation. There’s a little tab to pull on to open it. Once you open it, there is a protective cover over the cushion that you remove. Make sure to always push down the shelf part over top of the cushion completely so that the cushion doesn’t dry out.

This comes in 2 shades - “21 Light Beige,” which is described as “bright and glamorous light beige,” and “23 Natural Beige,” which is described as “natural and lively natural beige.” I have very fair skin so I can usually go for the lightest shade and can make it work for me. But, I wasn’t quite sure which would work best for me so I got both.

I took a photo of swatches I did. I did a photo showing a swatch of shade “23 Natural Beige,” “21 Light Beige,” and a comparison swatch of Maybelline Fit Me Matte+Poreless in 110 Porcelain. I always like to use the Maybelline Fit Me since I know a lot of people have tried it and hopefully know their shade in it so they can hopefully get an idea of if the shade will work for them when compared to the Maybelline shade.

“21 Light Beige” is lighter. Usually the lower number is the lighter one, but sometimes that’s not always the case because of undertone or just weird labeling. In my opinion, the swatches in the product photos are much lighter than they appear in person. I’d say that they are definitely at least a shade darker in person than they appear in the product photo. They both have yellow undertones.

They provide good, natural coverage and gives a glowy finish. It doesn’t transfer once it’s dries down, which is nice. I don’t even need to set it with powder. Since I have normal to dry skin, I prefer not to use powder where I don’t have to. But, with glowy foundations it’s usually needed. So, I like that I don’t need to with this! It doesn’t give full coverage, but can be built up to medium. If you use a the included sponge or a beauty sponge for application you can get light coverage with 1 layer, medium with 2 layers. If you use a brush for application you can get medium coverage with 1 layer, but I find it looks to heavy if you try to apply a second layer using a sponge. My preferred method is using a brush to apply a thin layer, and then going over it with a sponge to kind of make sure it’s all blended in nicely. Then, if any areas need additional coverage, I’ll use the sponge to add some additional product where I need it.

Overall, I think this is a really nice cushion foundation. If you don’t mind the chemical sunscreen ingredients, and like cushion foundations and a dewy finish, I think you’ll really like this!
